config.//: Logical server name. Prefixes every topic: <name>.<schema>.<table>.
config.//table.include.list: Explicit allow-list. A new table in the database does not start streaming by accident.
config.//plugin.name: pgoutput is Postgres' built-in logical decoding output plugin — no extension to install, unlike wal2json or decoderbufs.
config.plugin.name: pgoutput
config.publication.name: tideline_pub
config.//publication.autocreate.mode: The publication is created by init SQL, so Debezium must not try to manage it.
config.slot.name: tideline_slot
config.//snapshot.mode: initial: backfill existing rows as op='r', then stream. 'never' would silently skip everything already in the table.
config.//: Envelope is kept intact. No ExtractNewRecordState transform: the pipeline needs before-images, the LSN, and the snapshot flag, all of which unwrapping discards.
config.//tombstones.on.delete: Emit the null-valued tombstone after a delete, so a compacted topic can drop the key. The Spark job filters them.
config.//decimal.handling.mode: double keeps NUMERIC columns readable as numbers. The default, 'precise', emits base64-encoded bytes that every consumer then has to decode.
config.//time.precision.mode: connect maps timestamps to standard Connect logical types instead of Debezium's microsecond longs.
config.//heartbeat.interval.ms: Postgres cannot release WAL for a replication slot until the consumer acknowledges an LSN. On a low-traffic table the slot can pin WAL indefinitely and fill the disk. Heartbeats keep the acknowledged position moving.
config.//max.batch.size: Modest batches suit a laptop; raise on real hardware.
config.//topic.creation: Single-broker stack, so replication factor must be 1.
config.//errors.tolerance: Fail loudly. A silently skipped change event is a table that quietly diverges from its source.
config.//schema.history: Not required for the Postgres connector (unlike MySQL); schema comes from the WAL relation messages, which is what makes mid-stream ALTERs propagate automatically.
